approved: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
This bill would let the government set an annual fee for Australian companies that check whether medical devices are safe and well made.
It does this by allowing regulations to prescribe a charge for a conformity assessment body determination, which the Secretary can issue under the Therapeutic Goods Act.
The bill also makes minor changes to keep charging rules consistent when a determination is suspended and to apply annual charges to provisionally registered medicines listed under state laws.
Enables regulations to set an annual charge for conformity assessment body determinations.
Ensures the obligation to pay the annual charge continues during a suspension of the determination.
Extends annual charges to provisionally registered goods entered in the Register by Commonwealth officers under a corresponding state law.
Australian corporations that hold a conformity assessment body determination and sponsors of provisionally registered medicines.

Labor supported the Therapeutic Goods Amendment (2017 Measures No. 1) Bill and related bill, which implement reforms from the 2015 expert panel review, including provisional registration of new medicines, a new pathway for complementary medicines, and stronger postmarket monitoring. The speaker also cautioned about outsourcing TGA responsibilities and pledged to monitor the changes.
